metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map (Batch 4)

audit_results.title: Verify emergency state only triggered by divergent valid proofs

attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Emergency trigger at Verifier.sol:283-288 checks `existingRoot != 0 && existingRoot != newRoot` after proof verification passes via IRootDecider.verifyOpaqueNovaProof(). The input is the proof bytes decoded to uint256[32], validated by the external verifier. Cannot bypass verification to reach emergency trigger.
attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.evidence: Line 274: `require(IRootDecider($.rootDecider).verifyOpaqueNovaProof(proof_), InvalidProof())` - verification occurs BEFORE emergency check at line 283

attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.analysis: Emergency state transition requires: (1) proof passes verification, (2) existingRoot already stored for this index, (3) new root differs from existing. The state machine correctly guards against false emergency triggers since only valid proofs can reach the comparison.
attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.evidence: Line 282-288: existingRoot read from provedTransferRoots[newIndex], compared only if non-zero

attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.analysis: An attacker could potentially submit many proofs to different indices to fill storage, but this is limited by practical constraint of index values derived from zERC20 transfer indices which are monotonic. Each proof submission costs significant gas for verification.
attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.evidence: ZK proof verification is computationally expensive, rate-limiting attack surface

attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: Emergency trigger calls _pause() and emits EmergencyTriggered event, then returns early (line 287-288). This is intentional behavior, not a silent failure. The pause propagates to all whenNotPaused functions.
attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.evidence: Line 285-286: _pause() called, EmergencyTriggered event emitted with conflicting root values

attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.analysis: Two transactions with conflicting proofs for same index could race, but EVM atomicity ensures each transaction sees consistent state. The first to execute stores its root, second triggers emergency if root differs.
attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.evidence: EVM transaction atomicity prevents partial state; line 282-289 executes atomically

counterexample.description: Counterexample for emergency manipulation: Attacker submits proof P1 for index I, root R1 is stored. Attacker then submits proof P2 for same index I with different root R2.
preconditions: P1 and P2 are both valid proofs for index I
attack_steps: 1. Submit P1 for index I - R1 stored
2. Submit P2 for index I with R2 - triggers emergency
counterexample.expected_behavior: Emergency triggered because valid proofs disagree - this is CORRECT BEHAVIOR indicating ZK system bug
counterexample.actual_behavior: System correctly identifies proof disagreement and enters emergency state
counterexample.result: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REFUTED - This is the intended security mechanism

guards_identified: whenNotPaused modifier - prevents operations during emergency
existingRoot != 0 check - only triggers when root already exists
audit_results.notes: Emergency trigger logic is correct. The mechanism detects genuine ZK system bugs where two valid proofs produce different roots for the same hash chain checkpoint. NEEDS_VERIFICATION: Confirm IRootDecider implementation is sound.

audit_results.title: Verify teleport processing requires valid proof data submission

attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: teleport() at line 306-328 and singleTeleport() at line 336-350 both decode proof bytes via abi.decode. Empty proof would fail decoding. Proof verification via IWithdrawDecider/IWithdrawVerifier follows immediately.
attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.evidence: Line 313: `abi.decode(proof, (uint256[34]))` - empty/malformed proof fails decode; Line 325: verifyOpaqueNovaProof called

attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.analysis: State transition to teleport processing requires proof parameter. No path exists to _teleport() without proof validation.
attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.evidence: teleport() calls require(IWithdrawDecider..verifyOpaqueNovaProof(proof_), InvalidProof()) before _teleport()

attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.analysis: Empty proof reverts on decode, valid proof requires ZK verification which is expensive. No cheap DoS vector.
attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.evidence: abi.decode fails on empty/short bytes, verification costs significant gas

attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: InvalidProof() custom error reverts transaction cleanly. No silent failure paths.
attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.evidence: Line 325: require(..., InvalidProof()) - explicit revert on failure

attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.analysis: No race condition concern - each teleport is atomic and checks monotonicity via totalTeleported.

counterexample.description: Attempt teleport with empty proof bytes
preconditions: Attacker calls teleport with proof = bytes('')
counterexample.expected_behavior: Transaction reverts on abi.decode failure
counterexample.actual_behavior: Reverts with decoding error for empty bytes to uint256[34]
counterexample.result: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REFUTED - Empty proof cannot reach processing

audit_results.notes: Proof validation is enforced. Empty/malformed proofs fail at decode step before any state modification.

audit_results.title: Verify root reference validation checks both proved and global root mappings

attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _teleport() at line 356-383 validates root reference at lines 366-368. The isGlobal flag determines which mapping to check. Both globalTransferRoots and provedTransferRoots are validated.
attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.evidence: Line 366: `expectedRoot = isGlobal ? $.globalTransferRoots[rootHint] : $.provedTransferRoots[rootHint]`; Line 367: `require(expectedRoot != 0, ExpectedRootZero(rootHint))`

attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.analysis: Root validation occurs before any token minting. Cannot proceed to teleport completion without valid root reference.
attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.evidence: Lines 366-368 execute before line 381 IzERC20($.token).teleport() call

attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.analysis: Each root lookup is O(1) mapping access. No DoS vector from root validation.
attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.evidence: Single mapping read operations, bounded gas cost

attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: ExpectedRootZero(rootHint) custom error provides clear failure indication when root not found.
attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.evidence: Line 367: explicit require with descriptive error

attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.analysis: Root storage is monotonic (roots are added, never removed). A root that exists in block N will exist in block N+1.
attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.evidence: provedTransferRoots and globalTransferRoots only ever written, never deleted

counterexample.description: Attempt teleport with non-existent root reference
preconditions: rootHint points to empty slot in both mappings
counterexample.expected_behavior: Transaction reverts with ExpectedRootZero error
counterexample.actual_behavior: Reverts at line 367 when expectedRoot == 0
counterexample.result: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REFUTED - Cannot teleport against unproved root

guards_identified: isGlobal flag determines which root source to validate against
audit_results.notes: Root validation correctly checks both local (provedTransferRoots) and global (globalTransferRoots) mappings based on isGlobal flag.

audit_results.title: Verify recipient hash binds proof to msg.sender

attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _teleport() validates recipient at lines 370-374. The GeneralRecipient struct's hash is computed and compared. Chain ID binding at line 374 prevents cross-chain replay.
attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.evidence: Line 371: `expectedRecipient = gr.hash()`, Line 372: `require(recipient == expectedRecipient, RecipientMismatch(...))`

attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.analysis: Recipient validation occurs before minting. The gr.chainId check at line 374 ensures proof is bound to current chain.
attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.evidence: Line 374: `require(gr.chainId == localChainId, InvalidRecipientChainId(gr.chainId, localChainId))`

attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.analysis: gr.hash() is a single hash computation. No DoS vector.

attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: RecipientMismatch and InvalidRecipientChainId errors clearly indicate failure mode.
attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.evidence: Lines 372, 374: explicit require statements with descriptive errors

attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.analysis: Recipient hash is derived from calldata (gr) and block.chainid. No mutable state involved.

counterexample.description: Front-running attack: Attacker sees user's teleport transaction and tries to use same proof
preconditions: User U submits proof for recipient hash H derived from their GeneralRecipient
attack_steps: 1. Attacker extracts proof from user's pending tx
2. Attacker submits same proof with their own GeneralRecipient
counterexample.expected_behavior: Attacker's tx reverts because their gr.hash() != recipient from proof
counterexample.actual_behavior: RecipientMismatch error - proof is cryptographically bound to original recipient
counterexample.result: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REFUTED - Recipient binding prevents proof theft

audit_results.notes: CRITICAL SECURITY PROPERTY: Recipient hash binding prevents proof theft/front-running. The proof includes recipient hash as public input, cryptographically binding it.

audit_results.title: Verify monotonicity check prevents double-spend

attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Monotonicity check at line 376-377 uses strict inequality: `require(value > currentTotal, NothingToWithdraw(...))`. Cannot claim same value twice.
attack_vector_1_input_validation_bypass.evidence: Line 376: `currentTotal = $.totalTeleported[recipient]`; Line 377: `require(value > currentTotal, ...)`

attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.analysis: After minting, totalTeleported is updated atomically at line 379. No path to mint without updating counter.
attack_vector_2_state_transition_violati.evidence: Line 378-379: `diff = value - currentTotal; $.totalTeleported[recipient] += diff`

attack_vector_3_resource_exhaustion_dos.analysis: Monotonicity check is O(1) mapping read. No DoS vector.

attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: NothingToWithdraw(currentTotal, value) error clearly indicates replay attempt.
attack_vector_4_faulty_error_handling.evidence: Line 377: descriptive error with both values for debugging

attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.analysis: Two identical proofs submitted in parallel: first succeeds, second reverts due to updated totalTeleported.
attack_vector_5_race_conditions_concurre.evidence: EVM atomicity ensures totalTeleported update visible to second tx

preconditions: User has valid proof for value V
attack_steps: 1. Submit proof, receive V tokens, totalTeleported = V
counterexample.expected_behavior: Second submission reverts: value(V) > totalTeleported(V) is FALSE
counterexample.actual_behavior: NothingToWithdraw(V, V) - strict inequality prevents replay
counterexample.result: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REFUTED - Monotonicity check prevents double-spend

audit_results.notes: CRITICAL: Double-spend prevention via monotonic counter. The cumulative model (totalTeleported) combined with strict inequality ensures each value unit claimed exactly once.
